What do the Olympic rings and their colours mean?

Five rings, five colours and one common misconception. Here’s the story behind the Olympic symbol.

By Biel Sardà · Published 29 Sept 2026 · Suggest a correction

Does each colour represent a continent?

You may have learnt that each Olympic ring colour belongs to a different continent. It is a familiar explanation, but the International Olympic Committee says there is no official colour-to-continent match.

What the five rings represent

The interlocking rings represent the union of five continents and athletes coming together from around the world. Their meaning lies in the whole symbol, rather than in five separate colour labels.

Why these colours?

Pierre de Coubertin designed the rings in 1913. According to the IOC, blue, yellow, black, green and red, together with the white background, represented the colours found in the national flags of that time.

That makes the white background part of the design’s story too, even though it is easy to overlook.

A quick check

Which statement is correct?

  1. Each ring colour stands for a particular continent.
  2. The five rings together represent the union of five continents.
Show the answer

Statement 2. The rings express unity; the individual colours do not label continents.
